nodes.label: ARID1B
nodes.plain_language: ARID1B encodes a subunit of the BAF (SWI/SNF) chromatin-remodeling complex important in neurodevelopment.

nodes.label: ARID1B protein (BAF250b)
nodes.plain_language: Protein product of ARID1B that participates in BAF complexes.

nodes.label: Coffin-Siris syndrome 1 (CSS1)
nodes.genotype_scope: Heterozygous pathogenic ARID1B variant with CSS clinical framing
nodes.plain_language: A clinical CSS subtype linked to heterozygous ARID1B variants. Other BAF genes can also cause CSS — keep gene attributions separate.

nodes.label: ARID1B-related disorder (ARID1B-RD)
nodes.plain_language: Gene-centered umbrella used by advocacy and natural-history programs for ARID1B presentations ranging from CSS-like to less syndromic ID.
nodes.notes: Gene-centered collection ≠ automatic mechanistic disease cluster proof.

nodes.label: ARID1B-related nonsyndromic intellectual disability
nodes.plain_language: Intellectual disability presentations with pathogenic ARID1B variants without classic CSS physical framing.

nodes.label: ARID1B haploinsufficiency
nodes.plain_language: One functional gene copy is not enough for typical development. This is a disease-mechanism framing supported for heterozygous LoF patterns — not a claim that every predicted truncating variant has been experimentally proven loss-of-function in every tissue.

nodes.label: BAF (SWI/SNF) chromatin remodeling
nodes.plain_language: Chromatin remodeling that helps control which genes are accessible during development.

nodes.label: Intellectual disability (variable severity)
nodes.plain_language: Learning and adaptive challenges of variable degree across the ARID1B spectrum.

nodes.label: Fifth-digit / nail hypoplasia (CSS hallmark, variable)
nodes.plain_language: Underdeveloped or absent fifth fingernails/toenails is a classic CSS feature, but not required for every ARID1B-RD presentation.
uncertainties: Not all ARID1B pathogenic-variant carriers show classic nail findings.

nodes.label: Speech delay / limited speech
nodes.plain_language: Common developmental feature; severity varies.

nodes.label: ARID1B p.Arg1225Ter
nodes.clinical_significance: Pathogenic (ClinVar aggregate context; check current record)
nodes.plain_language: Representative heterozygous nonsense allele used as an example. Predicted consequence is not the same as a measured functional assay.

nodes.label: ARID1B c.4479G>A (splice)
nodes.predicted_molecular_consequence: synonymous-looking coding change at splice donor
nodes.experimentally_observed_effect: RNA studies report exon 17 skipping with frameshift/early termination
nodes.plain_language: Example where predicted coding consequence (synonymous) differs from experimentally observed splicing effect.

nodes.label: Heterozygous ARID1B LoF-class genotype (typical)
nodes.genotype_scope: One pathogenic ARID1B allele + one reference allele (typical de novo)
nodes.plain_language: Typical disease-associated genotype context is heterozygous, often de novo — not an HBB-style homozygous recessive genotype.

nodes.label: van der Sluijs et al. 2019 — ARID1B spectrum in 143 patients
nodes.plain_language: Compares ARID1B-CSS and ARID1B-ID ascertainment; reports mostly frameshift/nonsense variants and de novo origin when parents tested.

nodes.label: Hoyer et al. 2012 — ARID1B haploinsufficiency in ID
nodes.plain_language: Early evidence linking de novo heterozygous ARID1B LoF-class variants to intellectual disability via haploinsufficiency.

nodes.label: CARE4ARID1B natural history study
nodes.overall_status: Prospective multi-site natural history (public study description; verify enrollment status before citing as open/closed)
nodes.plain_language: Multi-country prospective natural-history study aiming to define developmental trajectories and clinical endpoints for ARID1B-RD.
nodes.does_not: Does not claim an approved disease-modifying treatment; observational natural-history design per public description.
nodes.access_info: Public study description pages; contact via study site channels. No participant-level data in this atlas.

nodes.label: Foundation for ARID1B Research (FAR)
nodes.access_info: Public website and contact email listed on site. Atlas does not contact anyone automatically.
nodes.plain_language: Parent-led foundation focused on ARID1B-RD research and translational collaboration.

nodes.label: CARE4ARID1B study design / endpoint framing
nodes.plain_language: Publicly described natural-history design (assessments, biomarkers, endpoint goals) useful as a research-planning reference.

nodes.label: Phenotypic modifiers beyond ARID1B genotype (open)
nodes.plain_language: Sources note variable expressivity and limited genotype–phenotype correlation — modifiers are plausible but not settled here.

nodes.label: Which natural-history endpoints are ready for interventional trial design in ARID1B-RD?
nodes.plain_language: Concrete next question connecting biology and CARE4ARID1B goals to collaboration planning — not a treatment recommendation.
uncertainties: Adult natural-history data remain limited per advocacy sources
Endpoint readiness may differ across CSS-like vs less syndromic presentations
No approved disease-modifying therapy is asserted in this atlas
validation_questions: Which CARE4ARID1B endpoints are sufficiently defined for a future interventional protocol discussion?
How should CSS1 vs broader ARID1B-RD framing change eligibility language?

edges.plain_language: ARID1B is a BAF (SWI/SNF) complex subunit gene.

evidence.supporting_passage: ARID1B is a member of the SWItch/Sucrose NonFermenting (SWI/SNF) chromatin-remodeling complex

edges.plain_language: BAF-complex dosage sensitivity frames why losing one ARID1B copy can disrupt developmental gene regulation.

evidence.supporting_passage: Haploinsufficiency: Sufficient Evidence for Haploinsufficiency (3)
evidence.limitations: Dosage curation summarizes many reports; not a single functional assay.

edges.plain_language: Haploinsufficiency is the primary disease-mechanism framing for ARID1B-RD.

evidence.supporting_passage: Among individuals with ARID1B-RD, only one copy of the ARID1B gene is not functional and the remaining functional copy is not enough to preserve normal function. This condition is termed haploinsufficiency
evidence.limitations: Advocacy page summarizing genetics; corroborate with peer-reviewed cohorts.

edges.plain_language: Heterozygous ARID1B LoF-class variants cause CSS1 via haploinsufficiency framing.

evidence.supporting_passage: Coffin-Siris syndrome-1 (CSS1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the ARID1B gene

edges.plain_language: CSS1 is a clinically framed subset within the broader ARID1B-RD spectrum language.

evidence.supporting_passage: Changes (variants) in the ARID1B gene are the most common cause of Coffin-Siris syndrome.
evidence.limitations: Does not imply every ARID1B-RD case meets classic CSS criteria.

edges.plain_language: Nonsyndromic ARID1B-ID and CSS1 share the gene but are kept as distinct clinical framings with overlapping biology.

evidence.supporting_passage: The associated phenotypes range from clearly recognizable Coffin–Siris syndrome (ARID1B-CSS) to less specific ID (ARID1B-ID).

edges.plain_language: Typical ARID1B-RD genotype context is heterozygous pathogenic variation.

evidence.supporting_passage: Although ARID1B-RD is a genetic disorder, it is very rarely inherited. Instead, pathogenic changes in the ARID1B gene occur as random events

edges.plain_language: Example genotype context can include a heterozygous nonsense allele.

evidence.limitations: Illustrative allele; not claiming this allele defines all ARID1B-RD.

edges.plain_language: p.Arg1225Ter is an allele of ARID1B.

evidence.supporting_passage: Gene: ARID1B

edges.plain_language: c.4479G>A is an allele of ARID1B.
ClinVar variation 31210 is the structured record for this allele example.
ClinVar variation 210291 is the structured record for the splice example.
Reported splice/RNA effect supports a LoF-class mechanism framing for this allele — still allele-specific evidence, not a universal rule.

evidence.supporting_passage: RNA studies, which show that this variant causes exon 17 to be skipped, resulting in a frameshift and early termination
evidence.experimental_context: RNA studies cited in ClinVar interpretation text
evidence.limitations: Do not generalize from this allele to all predicted truncating variants without transcript/NMD context (see PMID 38671509 caution).

edges.plain_language: Intellectual disability of variable degree is commonly reported in ARID1B-RD.

evidence.supporting_passage: Children and adults with ARID1B-RD typically have intellectual disability of variable degree
evidence.population_context: ARID1B-RD as described by FAR; severity variable

edges.plain_language: Fifth-digit/nail hypoplasia is a classic CSS feature (variable across spectrum).

evidence.supporting_passage: CSS is characterized by variable degrees of intellectual disability, speech impairment, coarse facial features, hypertrichosis, sparse scalp hair, and hypoplastic or absent fifth fingernails or toenails.
evidence.limitations: Hallmark of CSS framing; not mandatory for every ARID1B-ID presentation.

edges.plain_language: Speech delay or limited speech is commonly described.

evidence.supporting_passage: delays or (near) absence of speech

edges.plain_language: The 143-patient spectrum paper characterizes ARID1B clinical diversity.

evidence.supporting_passage: Pathogenic variants in ARID1B are one of the most frequent causes of intellectual disability (ID) as determined by large-scale exome sequencing studies.
evidence.population_context: n=143 patients with pathogenic ARID1B variants

edges.plain_language: Cohort includes ARID1B-CSS ascertained patients.

evidence.supporting_passage: ARID1B is by far the most frequently mutated gene (51–75%) in Coffin Siris syndrome (CSS) (OMIM 135900)
evidence.population_context: Percentage refers to mutation-positive share among CSS cohorts cited in the paper (refs therein), not a universal population rate.
evidence.reporting_basis: van der Sluijs et al. 2019 citing prior CSS sequencing series

edges.plain_language: Most pathogenic variants in the cohort were frameshift/nonsense; de novo when parents tested.

evidence.supporting_passage: Pathogenic variants were apparently de novo in all cases where parents could be tested (107/107). ... Most pathogenic variants were frameshift or nonsense (n = 118)
evidence.population_context: 107/107 de novo among parent-tested subset; 118 frameshift/nonsense
evidence.limitations: Does not prove every predicted truncating variant causes NMD/functional loss in every transcript context.

edges.plain_language: Hoyer 2012 linked de novo heterozygous ARID1B LoF-class variants to haploinsufficiency.

evidence.supporting_passage: Haploinsufficiency of ARID1B, a Member of the SWI/SNF-A Chromatin-Remodeling Complex, Is a Frequent Cause of Intellectual Disability
